title: Vireo Engine vs llama.cpp
headline: Vireo's own engine against llama.cpp, on a small laptop GPU
lede: Same GGUF files, same GPU, the Mac benchmark's three prompts and method. One token at a time, Vireo writes level with llama.cpp (93–111%), in a short chat and 30,000 tokens into one. It reads a 2,300-token prompt ahead of llama.cpp on the Gemmas and behind on the larger Qwens (79–87%), and a 30,000-token one at 78–84% on every model. As shipped, with guesses from the chat and Google's draft models, the Gemmas' whole replies come out 1.2 to 3.7 times as fast as llama.cpp's.

rig.label: Laptop
rig.detail: FA401GM · on mains, Turbo power plan, after a restart

rig.label: GPU
rig.detail: 8 GB · Blackwell, 26 SMs · driver 621.14 · 105 W limit

rig.label: Software
rig.detail: llama.cpp b12262 (CUDA build) · Vireo in 8-bit mode, main at 28ddaeb

method: How it was measured (evals/speed/bench_windows.py, after the Mac's prompts-mac/bench_mac.py, with its prompt files): short.txt (33–34 tokens, 128 written), medium.txt (~2,300, 64 written) and long.txt (27,000–34,000 by tokenizer, 64 written). The first four panels: no drafting, one engine and one model loaded at a time, two rounds with the engines' order reversed, the mean of the two; Vireo with vireo-cli generate --gpu, llama.cpp with llama-server -ngl 99 -fa on -c 36000 and the prompt to /completion with cache_prompt off, speeds from each engine's own timings. The last four panels are whole replies through each engine's server at temperature 0: vireo-server at its defaults against llama-server -c 8192, the same user message to each (tools/reply_speed.py's four), the second of two rounds. Every guessed token is checked by the model, so the text is what Vireo would write without guessing. Through its server Vireo also offers the model its tools: Qwen 3.5 4B answered the code request by calling one instead of returning the file, and Qwen 3.5 9B once asked to remember something (refused at once; a first run that left the approval unanswered is in superseded.jsonl). The laptop was restarted before the run: earlier the same day its GPU ran at a third to a half of these speeds. Llama 3.2 1B was measured too (in results.jsonl) and is left out here.
